subject: Clarify commit true-up, carryforward, and streaming token slab math
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia@acme-analytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Ford <mford@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question: token metering for streaming responses + commit language

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. As we prep the SOW and pricing exhibit, the procurement team has a couple of precise questions so our counsel can sign off:

1) For streaming responses (server-sent events / chunked), how are billable tokens measured? Do you meter per-token as they emit, or is there a per-request/time-window aggregation? We want to avoid surprises from long-lived streams that emit tokens intermittently.

2) Rounding: do you round per-request, per-stream-chunk, or at the aggregate invoice line? If per-request, rounding can add a non-trivial % on short responses.

3) Commit carryforward and true-ups: our finance team prefers a quarterly true-up and the ability to carry forward unused committed tokens for one billing period. Is that something Redwood supports, and if so are there limits (% of commit)?

4) Slab / marginal discounts: we need clarity on whether discounts are applied marginally (each additional token above a threshold gets the lower price) or on the whole bucket once you cross a tier.

Can you provide proposed contract wording for the above so our counsel can review? I attached the current SOW draft for context.

Thanks,
Julia
Procurement, Acme Analytics

Attachments: Acme_SOW_DRAFT_v3.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: token metering for streaming responses + commit language

Hi Julia — thanks, good questions. Summarizing at a high level, and I'll have Laura add formal wording and Ben can pull pricing tables. Quick answers:

• Metering: billable tokens = request tokens + response tokens produced by the model. For streaming, tokens are counted as they are emitted. We do not create a separate "streaming token" concept for billing; it flows into the same token counter.

• Rounding: our default is to aggregate tokens per customer per billing period and report/round the line-item total (this minimizes rounding overhead for customers). For customers that prefer per-request rounding for operational reasons we can include that in the contract but it's less common.

• Commit & true-up: we normally do monthly billing with a monthly commit bucket and a monthly true-up, but we can accommodate quarterly true-ups with a small admin surcharge. Carryforward of unused committed tokens is possible as a negotiated term (we typically allow up to 15% carryforward into the next billing period for a single cycle; larger carryforwards are handled as credits).

• Discount application: we support marginal (laddered) pricing so the marginal price applies to usage within each slab — most customers prefer this because it avoids cliff effects. If you need flat-rate-for-entire-bucket semantics we can put that in the exhibit, too.

I'm attaching a quick workbook with examples and a sample SOW clause that Laura can formalize. If you're open, Ben and I can propose two options: (A) monthly commit + monthly true-up + 15% carryforward; (B) quarterly true-up + 20% carryforward + small admin fee (0.5% of committed spend). Which is preferable?

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference

Attachments: token-accounting-math.xlsx, sample-sow-snippet.txt

From: Julia Park <julia@acme-analytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Ford <mford@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: token metering for streaming responses + commit language

Markus — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we loop legal:

• For streaming: any special-case token types (e.g., control frames, keep-alive heartbeats) that you exclude from billing?

• On rounding: we prefer the "aggregate per billing period and then round" approach — can you quantify the worst-case rounding delta as a percentage for our monthly volumes (we expect a steady 180M tokens/mo with spikes)?

• Carryforward: 15% is close to acceptable. Our CFO is pushing for 20% carryforward on a quarterly true-up cadence (not monthly).

If you can share specific proposed contract clauses (definition of Billable Token, Rounding Rule, Carryforward, True-Up timing) we can move faster. Also please indicate whether marginal slab pricing will be the default in the contract exhibit.

Thanks,
Julia

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia@acme-analytics.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed contract language: billable tokens, rounding, true-up, carryforward

Hi Julia — appreciate the clear questions. Below is language we can insert into the Master Services Agreement and Pricing Exhibit. I've kept it pragmatic and contract-ready; happy to iterate with your counsel.

Definitions
• "Billable Token": any unit of model input or output token as measured by Redwood's metering system. Billable Tokens include tokens generated by streaming responses and tokens consumed by requests.
• "Streaming Token": a Billable Token that is emitted by the model in a streaming response; Streaming Tokens are counted in the same manner as non-streaming response tokens for pricing and commit calculations.
• "Metering Period": the Customer's billing period (monthly unless otherwise agreed).

Rounding and Metering
• Aggregation: Redwood will aggregate all Billable Tokens for the Customer over the applicable Metering Period and compute the invoiceable quantity by summing measured tokens across requests and streams.
• Rounding Rule: The aggregated invoiceable quantity will be rounded to the nearest whole token for invoicing. Individual requests or streams are not rounded independently unless the Parties expressly agree. This approach limits per-request rounding exposure.
• Exclusions: Redwood does not bill control frames, connection keep-alives, or empty-heartbeat frames. Any additional event types to be excluded must be listed in an exhibit.

Commit, True-Up, and Carryforward
• Commit Period: The Customer may elect a Monthly or Quarterly Commit Term in the Pricing Exhibit.
• True-Up: For Monthly Commits, Units used above the committed quantity will be billed at the applicable marginal rate on the next invoice. For Quarterly Commits, Parties will perform a quarterly reconciliation (True-Up) within 15 days of quarter-end.
• Carryforward: Unused committed units may be carried forward for a single subsequent Metering Period up to 15% of the committed quantity by default. The Parties may increase the carryforward cap to 20% by selecting the Quarterly Commit Term and applying an administrative fee equal to 0.5% of committed monthly spend.

Discount Application
• Marginal (laddered) pricing shall apply by default. The unit price for tokens within each slab shall be applied to consumption in that slab. If Customer prefers bucket-level pricing (single price for entire usage after crossing a threshold), include the "Bucket Pricing" checkbox in the Pricing Exhibit.

Examples (illustrative)
• If Commitment = 100M tokens/month and Actual = 115M tokens: 100M billed at committed rate, 15M billed at next marginal slab rate. If Aggregated rounding adds 0.6 tokens total, it's rounded with the invoice line (negligible at scale).

If that wording looks good I'll add it to the SOW and Ben will update the pricing exhibit to show both Monthly and Quarterly commit options with the two carryforward alternatives.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: sample-sow-snippet.txt
